title: Share, Watched
summary: The Windows file server from Share and Tell, with file auditing switched on. Every file copied off the shared folder is noted, and so is every sign-in. Read only the one file you need.
story: Pinecone Logistics (made up) turned on file auditing on WIN-FS01 (10.10.3.40): copies from the Public share, connections to it and sign-ins are all counted, and wrong passwords count double. You start on scout. Get from the share to the administrator's desktop while touching as little as you can.
goal: Capture both flags on WIN-FS01 without raising the alarm, and keep the quiet bonus.
skills: SMB shares, listing before you copy, winrm-shell, credentials in scripts, staying quiet

defenderRules.watches: files copied off the shared folder, connections to it, sign-ins and especially wrong passwords

hints.text: This watcher is file auditing: each copy from the share costs a lot, each connection and sign-in a little, a wrong password a lot. Budget it: one listing of the shares, one connection that lists the folder and copies a single file, then two sign-ins with passwords you found.

smbclient -L //10.10.3.40 -N lists the shares; then in ONE connection list Public and get only the file that matters: smbclient //10.10.3.40/Public -N -c 'ls; get new-staff.txt'. The welcome file is not worth the noise.

winrm-shell -i 10.10.3.40 -u kim -p (the password from the note): kim's flag is on her desktop, and the script in her Documents holds the local Administrator password. Leave, then sign in once as Administrator for the last flag.
